mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when the trigger is met, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts contraction (HOUST) below 500k units for three consecutive months signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST < 500k for three months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 8% for two consecutive months, accompanied by a decline in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) for three consecutive months, signals deteriorating labor market conditions that depress corporate earnings and lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 8% for two months AND PAYEMS < previous month for three months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered instances, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals a broad-based contraction in economic activity that reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO declines for four months but S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of such periods, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid reduction in the federal funds rate below 1% during a financial stress episode (identified by RSAFS falling below 300 billion USD for two months) signals a liquidity-driven easing that boosts risk asset valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% AND RSAFS < 300 for two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above trend by more than 3% for six consecutive months signals a robust demand expansion that boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: GDPC1 above trend by more than 3% for six months but S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of such periods, or the average return is not significantly above zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the unemployment rate to below 5% while nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) rise for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market that increases wage pressure and inflation risk, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 5% AND PAYEMS increasing for three months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average by more than 4% for three consecutive months signals a supply-side expansion that boosts corporate revenues and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO above 12-month MA by more than 4% for three months but S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of such periods, or the average return is not significantly above zero at 95% confidence.
